messages:
Noura El-Khoury: ok team, social coordination thread for launch day. need: who posts when, which visuals are approved, and a quick response bank for early community qs. drop your handles + preferred slot.

Redwood Social Bot: Scheduled post reminder: "Benchmark Report Launch" campaign assets folder updated. Last sync: 2025-07-10 08:12 PT.

Soojin Lee: Thanks Noura. Canonical links for all posts:
- Landing page (interactive): https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar?utm_source=social&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_v1
- PDF download: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/report.pdf?utm_source=social&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_v1
- Methodology page: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/methodology?utm_source=social&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_v1
Please do NOT share any internal dashboards / raw sheets.

Camila Reyes: Brand account (@RedwoodInference) will go first. I want a clean, claims-safe post. No “fastest” / “best” / “#1” language. We lead with “production inference economics” and “latency/$” + link to methodology.

Ben Carter: For tracking, please use the UTM links Soojin posted. If you need a shortlink, DM me and I’ll generate one. Also: if you’re posting on LI, include the PDF link in comments (LI tends to downrank external links in the main body).

Alicia Perez: Approved visuals are in the “SOCIAL_FINAL” folder (same assets across LI/X). Please don’t use screenshots of the interactive table from staging.
Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RW-BENCH-SOCIAL_FINAL
Approved set:
1) "latency-per-dollar-hero.png" (1200x628)
2) "p95-heatmap.png" (square)
3) "region-consistency.png" (square)
4) "methodology-callout.png" (quote-style card)
Alt text drafts are in "alt-text-notes.txt" in the folder.

Wei Chen: +1. Also updated the landing page disclaimer copy yesterday; if anyone is quoting from the page, please pull fresh text.
Suggested one-liner to include in posts: “Details + reproducibility notes in the methodology section.”

Noura El-Khoury: Proposed posting schedule (PT). Please claim a slot:
- 08:30 PT: Brand (@RedwoodInference)
- 09:00 PT: Soojin (PMM)
- 09:30 PT: Ethan (blog angle)
- 10:00 PT: Jonas (technical / methodology)
- 11:00 PT: Camila (exec / why now)
- 12:30 PT: Ben (CTA / try it)
- 14:00 PT: EMEA-friendly repost (Lukas/Stephanie optional, or brand follow-up)

Soojin Lee: I can do 09:00 PT on LI and X.
Post framing:
- What we measured: latency/$ as a production economics lens
- Why it matters: cost predictability at p95, regional consistency
- CTA: interactive page + methodology

Ethan Wallace: I’ll take 09:30 PT. I’m going to focus on the “what surprised us” angle + 1 chart (hero). Will not name competitors.

Jonas Weber: I can do 10:00 PT (X mostly). Will emphasize:
- workload mix (prefill/decode) + concurrency
- repeated runs + variance gates
- links to methodology
No absolute “we win everywhere” claims.

Camila Reyes: I’ll take 11:00 PT. I’ll keep it high-level and point to the methodology.

Ben Carter: 12:30 PT works. I’ll include a clear CTA (“Try Hosted / talk to us about Dedicated/Private”) + mention there’s an export CSV on the page.

Tyler Benson: Adding guardrails for replies:
- If people ask “is this cherry-picked?” → point to methodology and that configs/workloads are published.
- If they ask “what about my workload?” → invite them to run a quick PoC; link methodology + offer to share harness guidance via DM.
- If they ask “what GPU / instance type?” → we can say “production-grade GPU fleet; details and constraints in methodology” (don’t post fleet composition publicly).

Soojin Lee: Dropping approved copy blocks (please don’t freestyle comparative language):
A) Short LI version:
“Today we’re publishing our benchmark report on production inference economics (latency/$) across models + regions. Interactive tables + full methodology included. We designed this to be reproducible and to reflect real prefill/decode mixes.
Read: <landing link>”
B) Short X version:
“Benchmark report is live: latency/$ across models + regions (plus p95 + $/1M tokens). Interactive page + methodology: <landing link>”

Sofia Mendes: Quick legal note (same as enablement):
- Avoid “outperforms X” unless you’re quoting the report’s exact scoped claim + include caveats.
- Don’t imply we tested “all providers” or “every region.”
- Don’t answer questions about competitor pricing assumptions beyond what’s in the public methodology.
If a thread gets spicy, route to PMM.

Michael Grant: +1. Also please don’t use the word “certified” (“Redwood-verified” is fine if it’s referencing our internal profiling process, but keep it vague). If you’re unsure, paste your draft here.

Grace O'Connor: Sales question: can we add “Dedicated and Private available” in comments? AEs want to tie this to data isolation / SLAs.

Soojin Lee: Yes, but keep it factual and not tied to benchmark numbers. Suggested comment:
“If you need dedicated capacity, VPC/private networking, or SLA-backed throughput/latency targets, Dedicated/Private options are available—happy to connect.”

Noura El-Khoury: Response bank draft (copy/paste). Please use as-is:
1) Q: “What is latency/$?”
A: “It’s a normalized view of end-to-end latency relative to serving cost, meant to reflect production economics. We also publish p50/p95, throughput, and $/1M tokens for context. Full definition + formulas here: <methodology link>.”
2) Q: “Did you enable caching/batching?”
A: “We used a consistent policy described in the methodology and focused on settings that reflect production defaults. Details (incl. warmup, caching policy, and exclusions) are documented here: <methodology link>.”
3) Q: “Can I reproduce this?”
A: “We designed it to be reproducible and included configs + run notes in the methodology. If you want to sanity-check with your workload, DM us and we can suggest a PoC setup.”
4) Q: “Why didn’t you include <model/provider>?”
A: “We started with a curated set and published our selection criteria + caveats. We’ll iterate—tell us what you’d like to see next.”

Jonas Weber: For technical replies, I can also add:
“If you’re comparing, match: prompt mix, concurrency, context length, and streaming vs non-streaming. Otherwise numbers will diverge.”

Wei Chen: Minor correction: we should avoid promising future updates on a schedule. Maybe “We may expand coverage over time” vs “we’ll iterate.”

Soojin Lee: Good catch. Update #4 to:
“We started with a curated set and published selection criteria + caveats. We may expand coverage over time—what would you like to see next?”

Alicia Perez: One more thing: LI image crop. Use the square charts for LI carousel. The 1200x628 hero is best for X + single-image LI.
Also: please include alt text on LI (accessibility + avoids “image contains text” complaints).

Ben Carter: Draft for my 12:30 PT post (paste for quick legal sanity):
“Benchmarks are live: latency/$ across models + regions, plus p95 latency and $/1M tokens. Explore the interactive tables, export the data, and see exactly how we ran it in the methodology.
<landing link>”

Sofia Mendes: Ben copy looks fine. Suggest adding “production inference economics” after “Benchmarks are live” and removing “exactly” (sounds like overpromise).

Ben Carter: updated:
“Benchmarks are live: production inference economics (latency/$) across models + regions, plus p95 latency and $/1M tokens. Explore the interactive tables, export the data, and see how we ran it in the methodology.
<landing link>”

Camila Reyes: Great. Also: if anyone asks about “why latency/$ not tokens/sec?” reply:
“Tokens/sec is useful, but it’s incomplete without cost and tail latency. We publish multiple metrics; latency/$ is meant to be a simple production economics lens.”

Noura El-Khoury: If you get press/analyst DMs from your post, don’t engage 1:1 on details—route to Ethan/Camila. We’re under embargo for partner newsletter until tomorrow 9am PT.

Soojin Lee: One more reminder: If someone claims “your benchmark is biased,” do not debate in-thread. Reply once with methodology link + invite them to review, then stop.

Jonas Weber: +1. I’ll keep my replies to: methodology link + scope + “happy to compare notes if you match workload.”

Noura El-Khoury: Cool. Final checklist:
- Use approved visuals only
- Use UTM links
- No comparative superlatives
- Route spicy threads to PMM
Drop your final drafts here if you want quick eyes.

Ethan Wallace: Here’s my 09:30 draft:
“Shipping LLM features is an economics problem as much as a model problem. We benchmarked latency/$ (plus p95 + $/1M tokens) across models + regions and published the methodology so you can see what we measured.
Interactive: <landing link>”

Michael Grant: Ethan draft is fine.

Noura El-Khoury: Locked. I’ll post the schedule + asset link in #announcements in 10. :thumbsup:
